Do I need to worry about lead paint here?

Usually not here. Frankfort is young by the standards of everywhere else on this site, mostly 2000s construction, and past 1978 the lead paint question stops being the first thing anyone has to plan around.

Age stops being the problem and reach starts. The stock is big: tall rooms inside, large uninterrupted walls outside, and one original coat across all of it. Surface preparation and getting safely to the work are what a quote on Frankfort housing turns on.

The Census publishes a pre-1980 bucket rather than a pre-1978 one, and on that measure 23.9 percent of the housing sits on the older side of the line in Frankfort. Low, on this list. Most of Frankfort went up after the 1978 line, which takes the lead-safe question off the table for most addresses in town instead of leaving it hanging over the quote.

None of that settles your own address. A median is a midpoint rather than a floor, and an older pocket inside a newer town is ordinary. Check the year.

What decides the price of a job in Frankfort

On housing built around 2000, the original finish was sprayed once at the factory or once on site and has never been touched. That gives a very consistent surface and a very unforgiving one: it fails all at once across a whole elevation rather than in patches, so the work is scheduled by elevation rather than by room. 13.9 percent of the housing here is attached, so a fair share of the work is townhome and association work: matching an existing scheme exactly, working to a board's schedule and painting several identical units in a row.

The lines a quote for Frankfort needs to show

  • Distance, stated. Frankfort is 16.5 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Frankfort is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Trim, counted separately. At a median of 8.1 rooms, casing, baseboard and doors are the half of an interior that actually varies. A single number for the whole house hides it.
  • Whole elevations. 81.7 percent of the housing is detached, so an exterior here is four sides and a garage rather than one face of a shared building.
  • Matching, exactly. 13.9 percent of units are attached, and on a shared elevation close is not good enough. Existing color has to be matched rather than approximated.

There are 6,922 housing units in Frankfort. 10.7 percent were finished before 1970 and 23.9 percent before 1980, against a median build year of 2000 and a median size of 8.1 rooms. That combination is the whole brief for a quote here.

Frankfort is 94.7 percent owner occupied, 6,244 households against 346 renting. 4.2 percent of units are in buildings of two or more, 13.9 percent are attached, and the remaining 81.7 percent are detached houses averaging 8.1 rooms. Median value across that stock is $461,600.

Frankfort is in the top four of the 54 suburbs and towns covered here for the largest homes by room count (8.1 rooms, first of them all), the newest housing by median build year (2000, first of them all) and the highest median home value ($461,600). It is also near the top for the highest owner-occupied share (94.7 percent), the newest housing stock overall (23.9 percent built before 1980) and the smallest share built before 1970 (10.7 percent).

Three figures put Frankfort a long way from the average of the 76 places on this site: housing in buildings of two or more at 4.2 percent against a 29 percent average, townhomes and rowhouses at 13.9 percent against a 7.5 percent average and housing built before 1970 at 10.7 percent against a 56.9 percent average.

Source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2019-2023 (tables B25003, B25024, B25034, B25035, B25077). Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Questions

Asked about Frankfort

Most of Frankfort is owner occupied. Does that change anything?

It changes what the work usually is. At 94.7 percent owner occupied, with 6,244 owner households, there is very little turnover painting here and a lot of repeat maintenance: exteriors on a cycle, one room at a time inside, trim and doors when they finally go. A maintained house and a neglected one are different jobs and should be different numbers, in both directions.

My house in Frankfort is not old. Why does the quote still take so long?

Height and area, mostly. Housing here runs to a 2000 median build year, which means two story elevations outside and two story entries and stair walls inside. That is access equipment and setup time rather than paint, and it is the part that gets left out of a fast number. It is worth having it itemized so you can see what you are paying for.

How is an interior price worked out for a house this size?

By trim, mostly. The median home in Frankfort runs 8.1 rooms, and rooms bring door casing, window casing and baseboard with them. Wall area is the fast part of an interior job and trim is the slow part, so a quote that gives one number for the whole house is hiding the half of it that actually varies. Ask for the trim separately.

Do you actually come out to Frankfort, or is this just a page?

It is 16.5 straight-line miles from the shop in Bridgeview, so it is a genuine drive and the answer depends on the job. A full exterior or a whole interior is worth the trip. One small patch on its own usually is not, and you will be told that rather than quoted a number that quietly covers the travel. Call 708-935-4289 and ask before you plan around it.
